extracted.intended_audience: AHRQ grant applicants and peer reviewers (health services researchers submitting or reviewing AHRQ grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and scoring guidance used by AHRQ peer review panels to assess the scientific and technical merit of health services research grant applications. Covers the five core scored criteria, agency-specific expectations (priority populations, implementation, stakeholder engagement), and scoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the health services research question; Potential to advance understanding of healthcare delivery; Relevance to AHRQ priorities (quality, safety, equity, accessibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project addresses an important problem in health services research and whether outcomes are likely to have meaningful impact on healthcare delivery or AHRQ priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifications of PI and team; Track record in health services research; Multi-disciplinary expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the expertise, past performance, and complementary skills of the principal investigator and key personnel, including evidence of productivity and ability to execute the proposed work. Consider whether the team composition supports the aims (multidisciplinary where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel approaches to healthcare research; New methodologies; Innovative use of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the degree to which the application challenges current paradigms, applies novel concepts or methods, or uses data sources in new ways that could lead to important advances in health services research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of methodology; Appropriate study design; Data sources and quality; Analysis plan; Implementation feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the research design and methods are rigorous and appropriate to the aims, whether proposed data sources are adequate and of sufficient quality, whether analysis plans are detailed and suitable, and whether the proposed study can feasibly be implemented as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional resources; Access to data, populations; Collaborations with healthcare delivery systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, availability of necessary resources and infrastructure, access to relevant study populations or data, and the strength of partnerships (e.g., with delivery systems) that will enable successful completion of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring System
rubrics_metrics.description: 9-point scale: 1 (exceptional) to 9 (poor); Score of 5 considered average; Final overall impact score = average × 10; Final scores range from 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 9-point numeric scale when assigning criterion scores. Panel procedures compute an overall impact score by averaging individual reviewers' scores and multiplying by 10 to produce a 10–90 scale for final ranking/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Populations Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers assess the adequacy of plans to address the needs of AHRQ priority populations and must include their assessment of the proposed inclusion plan for priority populations in evaluating the overall scientific and technical merit of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must propose and justify plans to address AHRQ priority populations. Reviewers should evaluate the completeness and appropriateness of inclusion plans and the extent to which the study will generate knowledge relevant to these groups. AHRQ priority populations include: low-income groups; minority groups; women; children; elderly; individuals with special healthcare needs; individuals living in inner-city and rural areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Science Focus / Translation to Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on translation of research to practice, real-world implementation, and evaluation of practice change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many AHRQ grants prioritize studies that move findings into practice. Reviewers should consider the strength of plans for translation, implementation strategies, measurement of implementation outcomes, and how the project will evaluate and support practice change in real-world settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement of stakeholders (including healthcare delivery systems) is often expected and valued by AHRQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the extent and meaningfulness of stakeholder engagement plans: whether stakeholders are appropriately identified, their roles are well-defined, and engagement is likely to enhance relevance, feasibility, uptake, or dissemination of findings. Strong collaborations with delivery systems are a positive factor under Environment and implementation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness and Economic Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-effectiveness sometimes evaluated as part of AHRQ reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers may assess economic analyses or cost-effectiveness components, judging whether methods are appropriate, data for costs are robust, and results will inform decision-making about value and scalability of interventions.
